measurement_scope: planned open-loop client arrival through authenticated HTTP response, Rust FlatBuffer serialization, System V shared-memory handoff, parser-enabled C++ FRTX verification, continuous batching, CPU reference handling, and response receipt; not GPU or production-model inference
aggregation: one seeded observational integration run with 15,000 scheduled arrivals

model.bundle_sha256: not applicable: deterministic CPU reference handler
model.numeric_backend: authenticated HTTP + parser-verified FRTX FlatBuffers + System V IPC + CPU reference
model.transaction_verification: parser-enabled FlatBuffers verification of the FRTX identifier, table bounds, required strings, and request metadata

limitations: CUDA Graph initialization was unavailable and the daemon used its CPU reference handler; this run contains no GPU measurements.
The GitHub-hosted runner is shared virtualized hardware, so this is reproducibility evidence rather than a production SLO or capacity claim.
Restricted kernel symbols and frame-pointer unwinding produced unknown frames; the FlameGraph SVG labels accumulated perf period weights as samples, so those labels are not literal event counts.
The flame graph represents sampled CPU time, not latency attribution, memory allocation tracing, or proof that every hot-path operation is allocation-free.
Only the C++ daemon was sampled; Rust gateway and Go client CPU costs are outside the flame graph.
